video.title: Is Coding Required for DevOps? Programming Usecases in Devops

transcript.text: One of the most asked questions by
people learning DevOps is how much
programming do I need to know or what
programming languages should I learn for
DevOps. So in this video I will explain
you how much coding is actually needed
in DevOps, what languages are useful and
also tell you where you will use this
programming languages in your DevOps
role. So let's get started.
Some of you might be confused if you
need to be a developer to do DevOps
task. The answer is no. Because in
DevOps, we don't create front-end UIs or
complex back end. Instead, as a DevOps
engineer, you will be automating the
software delivery process, managing
infrastructure, and making sure
everything is running smoothly. So in
DevOps you will use programming
languages to automate repetitive task
like provisioning servers installing
application also deploying code to
production without any manual step
creating infrastructure using code
creating CI/CD pipelines. So yes as a
DevOps engineer you will have to write
code but it's not like being a software
engineer where you create the entire
application it will be task specific
scripting and automation. So understand
that coding in DevOps is going to be
used to connect different tools speed up
process but not to create the entire
application. This means coding is
required in DevOps. But let me tell you
how much programming knowledge is enough
for you as a DevOps engineer. You don't
need to be a software engineer, but you
should be comfortable with writing
scripts to automate common tasks that
you do every day. You should also be
able to understand the code snippets and
logs whenever there's an issue. So you
can easily troubleshoot or modify
different kind of codes which could be
pipeline code, configuration code or
infrastructure code. Lastly, as a DevOps
engineer, you will also be working with
different APIs and different third party
tools. So, you need to understand how
APIs work and how to use them. Here is
an example. So, let's say you have an
application which is a microservices
application and you deploy a Docker
container on AWS. Whenever a developer
makes a change to this Docker container,
you want to automate the process to
automatically pull the image, push the
image and deploy the application. So to
do this you will use Python to create a
script or you might use a CI/CD tool
like GitHub actions. For Python you need
Python programming language knowledge
and for CI/CD tool you will need to have
YAML programming language knowledge. So
let's understand what are most common
programming languages used in DevOps. So
the most common languages include
different languages starting with bash
or shell scripting. So bash is the
language that is used in Linux systems
to automate different task. So you can
see bash is your go-to language when
working on Linux systems. You can use
bash or shell scripting for bootstrap
scripts or startup scripts for your EC2
or cloud servers. You can also create
bash scripts to automate your backups
for your databases. Bash scripts to
create chron jobs to do schedule task
and also for performing log files
cleanup or monitoring. Here's an example
of using bashcript to automate server
updates or restart a service if it
crashes. Another most used programming
language in DevOps is Python. So, Python
is the most beginner friendly and
powerful scripting language and we use
it in DevOps to write automation tools
and scripts. We also use it to talk to
different cloud providers like AWS,
Azure, GCP. In AWS, you can use Python
using the boto3 module. So, using boto3,
you can talk to AWS using Python
programming language. Uh you can use
Python to create Lambda functions in the
cloud or other serverless code.
Additionally, if you want to create a
tool in your own internal company, you
can use Python to create internal CLI
tool or dashboard. Here's an example of
how you can use Python script to detect
unused EC2 instances and shut them down
to save cost in your AWS. Similarly, you
can also automate different types of
task. Maybe you are changing password
for your databases and you want to
automate this process. You can use
Python for it or you can use bash as
well. Along with this, there's also YAML
and JSON. YAML and JSON are two
different languages that we use a lot in
DevOps. So I haven't mentioned Yam JSON
here but JSON is also another language
that we use a lot. So YAML is used
generally for Kubernetes manifest file
to create deployment service ingress
etc. It is also used with other DevOps
tools like GitHub actions, GitLab,
CI/CD, anible playbook and to create or
define Teraphform modules. Whereas JSON
is also similarly used in to create IM
policies. All the data that is stored in
DevOps tools are generally stored in
JSON language. So it's very important
for you to understand YAML and JSON as
well which might not be a programming
language but they are used in DevOps
everywhere. So YAML is like a language
of DevOps tools. You must understand how
to write and debug it. Example could be
defining how your application should run
inside a Kubernetes cluster by defining
deployment manifest in YAML language.
Lastly, Golang is another very much used
programming language in DevOps. If you
are someone who's trying to learn
programming language for DevOps, you
should consider Golang because every new
DevOps tool that we look at, let's say
Kubernetes, Terraform, Docker, all of
them are created in Golang. So, Golang
use cases could be contributing to open
source DevOps tools because mostly all
these DevOps tools are created in
Golang. You can also use Golang to
create custom Kubernetes operator. You
can use Golang to create fast CLI tools
or exporters for Prometheus. So example
of using Golang is if you want to build
a new plug-in for Terraform or modify
Kubernetes internals, Golang is the
language that you can use. Okay. So far
I've given you different examples of how
programming languages are used in
DevOps. But let's look at some more real
DevOps use cases where you will have to
write code. So you will have to write
bash script to restart a crashed
application or a server. You might be
asked to create a Python script to
upload logs to S3 or trigger a genkins
job. Generally something that you do
every day can be automated through
script. Uh you can also be asked to
create Kubernetes manifest file using
YAML language. So write YAML for
Kubernetes deployment or GitHub actions
workflow. You might be asked to
contribute to a go patch to open source
DevOps tool like Helm. Uh so you need to
know Golang language for that. And maybe
if you are someone who knows NodeJS
language, you might be asked to use
NodeJS to write an alert handler that
send messages to Slack channel. So
lastly understand that programming in
DevOps is used to automate repetitive
task. It is used to debug and modify
existing scripts and you should know
programming languages to understand how
these DevOps tools work behind the
scenes. Also programming languages is
used to glue together all the different
API scripts and configuration files. So
in a nutshell you will be using
programming languages not to build the
product but you will be using it to
build the pipeline that delivers the
product. So as a DevOps engineer, you
use programming languages not to create
the application but to automate the
process of building, configuring and
managing it. I hope this makes sense.
All right. So this was our video to help
you understand how much coding is
required in DevOps. I hope this video
